samples.question: This picture contains exactly one large square panel with a solid dark border, plus a few much smaller dark specks scattered on the background outside it that are decoration only. The panel's border encloses an eleven-by-eleven grid of 121 equal square cells; each cell is entirely dark, in the same tone as the border, or entirely pale, in the same tone as the panel's background. The dark cells form one thick solid blob. Carry out this operation on that grid, and only then read the answer. Peel one layer off the blob: delete every dark cell that touches a pale cell or touches the outside of the grid, counting a touch at a shared corner as well as a touch along a shared edge. Equivalently, keep a dark cell only when all eight cells surrounding it are dark cells of the grid, and delete every other dark cell. Delete them all at once, judging every cell against the grid as it is drawn rather than against the partly peeled grid. The cells that survive this single peel form exactly one of these four figures, described with the rows numbered 0 to 10 from the top of the grid and the columns numbered 0 to 10 from its left. 'bars' is two horizontal bars of five cells lying four rows apart: row 2 from column 2 to column 6, and row 6 from column 4 to column 8. 'pipes' is two vertical bars of five cells lying four columns apart: column 3 from row 2 to row 6, and column 7 from row 4 to row 8. 'tee' is a horizontal bar of five cells in row 3 from column 3 to column 7, with a vertical bar of five cells hanging from the middle of it, in column 5 from row 4 to row 8. 'corner' is a horizontal bar of five cells in row 4 from column 4 to column 8, with a vertical bar of five cells descending from its left end, in column 3 from row 4 to row 8, so the two bars meet at a square corner. Each figure is exactly ten cells, and every two of them differ in at least twelve cells. Whichever figure is hidden, the panel as drawn always carries exactly fifty dark cells, and those dark cells always fill the same bounding rectangle, from row 1 to row 9 and from column 1 to column 9, leaving the outermost ring of cells entirely pale. Neither the amount of dark ink, nor the extent of the blob, nor the panel's size, position or colour therefore reveals the figure. The blob as drawn is not any of the four figures and does not contain one that is readable without the peel: only the peel reveals it. Which figure do the surviving cells form? Answer with exactly one of: bars, corner, pipes, tee.
